title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The umbrella class to whom the whole policy applies: Key Management Personnel (including any director, executive or otherwise), nominated Employees and contractors, and Connected Persons of both. All substantive prohibitions (Blackout Periods, Additional Periods, hedging, margin loans and other secured lending, short term or speculative trading, non-discretionary trading plans) apply to this class without differentiation; only the identity of the Approving Officer differs.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: A person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any director (whether executive or otherwise). Distinguished only for clearance (Chair, or in his/her absence the Managing Director).

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: An employee or contractor of the Group nominated by the Managing Director or Company Secretary from time to time as a person to whom the Policy applies. Distinguished only for clearance (Managing Director, or in his/her absence the Company Secretary).

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: The Managing Director in his or her own personal dealing capacity; distinguished only for clearance (the Chair or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee).

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board in his or her own personal dealing capacity; distinguished only for clearance (the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee).

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18 years, a parent, an unlisted body corporate which the KMP or Employee controls or is a director of, a trust of which the KMP or Employee is a trustee and of which he or she or any of those persons is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom the KMP or Employee has significant influence or control. The KMP or Employee must procure the Connected Person to comply.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose an 'Additional Period' from time to time, for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure to the market but for Listing Rule 3.1A. It is confidential: 'Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect'.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule, but Company Securities expressly include derivatives of shares and rights, naming hedges and over-the-counter options, cash-settled or otherwise. To 'trade' includes applying for, acquiring or disposing of, or agreeing to apply for, acquire or dispose of, those securities, and section 7 requires prior written clearance for trading in Company Securities at any time. So writing a call and buying a put OTC over PLS shares requires prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer and is barred in a Prohibited Period absent exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities)

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over Company Securities are treated identically to OTC options; the definition of Company Securities draws no venue distinction and both are caught by the section 7 clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme. Unvested LTI/STI rights therefore cannot be collared or pledged.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of a security holding in the Company is expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer. The policy does not ban hedging of vested or on-market holdings outright; it converts it into a clearance decision. Clearance is valid five business days unless the Approving Officer states otherwise.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: The policy's only division is vested versus unvested entitlements; it does not separately address shares that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or disposal restriction. Where the entitlement is still 'unvested' in substance because performance or service conditions remain, the absolute ban applies; a holding-locked but fully vested share falls under the clearance limb instead.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar limits the economic risk of the holding and so falls under section 10, and to the extent it is secured on the shares it also falls under section 11. Either way it is permitted only with prior written clearance, and any accompanying agreement to dispose is itself 'trading'.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. A short sale of Company Securities is inherently short term and speculative trading, which section 9 bans outright, and it would in any event be a disposal requiring prior written clearance under section 7.
rules.evidence: Therefore, Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned, are not within the definition of 'trade' (apply for, acquire, dispose, or agree to do so), and are not caught by sections 10 or 11. A stock loan to the bank as part of a collar structure is unregulated by this policy, though the Company Secretary should be consulted.

CFDs are not named but an equity swap over Company Securities is expressly a Company Security, so acquiring one is trading requiring prior written clearance. In practice a CFD would also engage the section 9 ban on short term or speculative trading and, if short, the same objection as short selling.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loans over Company Securities are not banned; they require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer. A disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions in section 5, so a forced sale does not itself breach the policy.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company Securities is not itself listed as 'trading', but section 11 catches any secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities and requires prior written clearance. A charge or pledge unconnected with a lending arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities

rules.detail: Any secured lending in relation to Company Securities, not only margin lending, is permitted with prior written clearance. No security-state carve-out is stated for the loan itself, although section 10 separately bars limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements. The clearance decision is at the Approving Officer's discretion and no criteria are given.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: A bare, undefined prohibition on short term or speculative trading, expressed as an encouragement to adopt a long term attitude to investment. No holding period, no LIFO rule, no carve-outs and no numerical threshold are stated, so the boundary is a matter for the Approving Officer.
rules.evidence: The Company wishes to encourage Restricted Persons to adopt a long term attitude to investment in Company Securities. Therefore, Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

A circumstance may be considered exceptional if the person in question is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell, or accept a transfer of, the Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for him or her to do so.

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel / Chair (directors): trigger is any change in Company Securities held directly or indirectly, including changes arising from secured financing; to the Company Secretary; as soon as reasonably possible. Directors are separately reminded of the s205G Corporations Act 14-day notification obligation.

external_documents: Company form entitled 'Request for Prior Written Clearance to Trade in Company Securities'
exemption_authority: The relevant Approving Officer (section 7) may grant prior written clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period where the circumstances are exceptional (severe financial hardship, court order or other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, or any other circumstance the Approving Officer deems exceptional). The same Approving Officers grant clearance for hedging, margin loans and other secured lending, and non-discretionary trading plans. There is no Board-level waiver of the absolute ban on hedging unvested entitlements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is required for every leg of a funded collar at any time of year, not just in Blackout Periods, so entry, roll, unwind and physical settlement each need a fresh written approval.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lending is permitted with clearance
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a flat ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permissible here provided the Approving Officer gives prior written clearance, which makes a funded collar structurally available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs over vested shares are a clearance decision rather than a prohibition, so the whole structure turns on the Chair's or Managing Director's willingness to approve.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Absolute with no clearance route, so the collar and any security must be confined to shares that have already vested and been delivered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the section 5 restrictions].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale over the collared shares in a Blackout Period does not put the executive in breach, which removes the single biggest obstacle most ASX policies present to a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of five business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced, documented and executed inside five business days unless the Approving Officer expressly extends the window in the clearance itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board from time to time ... Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed Additional Period can block execution or unwind of the collar at any time, and the executive cannot even tell the bank why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the end of each of the March and September financial quarters and 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly reports for those financial quarters
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a mining company PLS has four closed periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undefined, so a short-dated or knock-out collar risks being characterised as speculative; a multi-year tenor with no early termination triggers is safer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs are themselves Company Securities, so acquiring the put and writing the call are separately 'trading' events needing clearance and falling outside Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirement; the executive must procure compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Breach of this policy (irrespective of whether the insider trading prohibition or any other law is breached) will also be regarded by the Group as serious misconduct which may lead to disciplinary action and/or dismissal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Executing any collar leg without written clearance is a dismissal-level offence, so the bank should condition drawdown on sighting the clearance.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, subject to discretionary approval. Section 10 permits transactions that limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's holding, and section 11 permits margin loans and other secured lending in relation to Company Securities, in each case only with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer (the Chair for a director or KMP, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair, the Managing Director for nominated Employees). The structure must be confined to vested shares, because limiting the economic risk of unvested equity scheme entitlements is prohibited absolutely with no clearance route. Execution must fall outside the four Blackout Periods (half-year, annual and the March and September quarterly reports) and any confidential Board-imposed Additional Period, must not be done while holding Inside Information, and must be completed within the five business days for which clearance is valid unless the Approving Officer states a longer period. Helpfully for the bank, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions, so enforcement over the collared shares does not breach the policy, although a short tenor or early-termination features could still fall foul of the undefined ban on short term or speculative trading.
